analysis.title: Tracking U.S. Supply Chain Congestion: GS Supply Chain Congestion Scale, Nov 16th; Index Slightly Higher W/W, Bottleneck Scale Unchanged at '2'
key_insights: The weekly bottleneck scale was unchanged at 2 (1 is fully open, 10 is fully bottlenecked) for the week of 11/16/2026. The congestion index rose +1% w/w.
Container ships waiting to dock on the West Coast rose from 1 to 3. East and Gulf Coast backlogs rose from 3 to 4.
West Coast rail intermodal traffic growth accelerated to +15% YoY on average, from +8% the prior week. BNSF was +9.7% YoY (vs -0.4%) and UNP was +20% YoY (vs +17%).

Rail service metrics were more improved than deteriorated. UNP terminal dwell fell from 19.8 to 19.6 hours, while BNSF dwell rose from 22.7 to 23.1 hours. Intermodal velocity was -4.3% YoY at UNP (vs -7.9%) and -5.6% at BNSF (vs -5.9%).
Ocean container rates from China/East Asia to the US West Coast were about $8.25k per FEU, down ~1% w/w from ~$8.34k. They were +179% YoY, versus +317% YoY the prior week.
Chassis street dwell was unchanged at 4.0 days for 20ft chassis and 5.9 days for 40/45ft chassis, and is well below peak congestion levels.

Lagged September data was mixed. Container weighted average dwell at San Pedro Bay rose to ~3.2 days from ~3.0, and rail container dwell rose to 7.2 days from 6.8 but stays far below the ~16-day 2022 peak.
Big Three West Coast ports (LA, Long Beach, Oakland) inbound loaded containers were +23% YoY in September.

Door-to-door shipping from China to the US averaged 47 days in October versus 46 in September, close to pre-pandemic transit times and well below the 80+ day peak. GS assumed unchanged transit times for index updating because the data provider gave limited updates.
LMI transportation capacity fell to 34.4 in September from 40.0, indicating faster contraction. Warehouse capacity was 39.3 (down from August) and warehouse utilization rose to 64.3 from 59.6.
Truck transportation employee count was about 4% below pre-Covid highs in September, but September marked the first positive YoY growth in 40 months.

GS says the key open question is how tariffs and geopolitical conflicts will affect demand and timing of freight flows. If pressures keep easing, the index could stay more consistently in '1' territory in 2026.
The combined weekly plus monthly scale averaged 124 in September, a bottleneck score of 2 but close to 1 when all metrics are combined.

sector_views.rationale: The note flags transport subsectors to watch while congestion remains muted but gives no overweight or underweight call.
